subject.title: fix(memory-core): honor private-network settings for OpenAI-compatible embeddings

question: Should configured memory embeddings trust only the exact configured origin when `request.allowPrivateNetwork` is omitted, fail closed and skip local-service probing when it is false, and allow broader private-network requests when it is true?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent and well proven, but these SSRF and compatibility semantics are an intentional product/security contract that automated review cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve the three-state contract
options.body: Land the PR with exact-origin trust by omission, explicit-denial fail-closed behavior, and explicit broader private-network opt-in.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in only
options.body: Block all private endpoints unless `request.allowPrivateNetwork` is true, then update the implementation, tests, docs, and proof.

options.title: Keep current restriction
options.body: Do not apply provider private-network policy to memory embeddings and continue requiring a relay for private endpoints.

recommendation.title: Approve the three-state contract
recommendation.body: Land the PR with exact-origin trust by omission, explicit-denial fail-closed behavior, and explicit broader private-network opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest cross-cutting history signal spans the provider request resolver, transport policy, shared SSRF helpers, and embedding-provider path needed to decide the permanent contract.
